IM10-01.why: 10, 15 and 30 form a related cluster (10x3, 30/2); a stem that says 'distinct' implies a with-repetition counterpart that is strictly larger, so the smallest member of the cluster is the one the qualifier selects.

IM10-02.why: 54 and 108 are an exact halving pair and the counting formula the stem's shape implies ends in a division by 2, so 108 is the forgot-to-halve partner and cannot itself be the count.

IM10-03.why: 650000 is the odd one out by form - the other three are clean powers of ten, which is what a product of two scientific-notation values with a round mantissa product must be; among the three powers of ten nothing in the option set picks one.

IM10-04.why: All four options are category values from the table's first column, so every one of them is a legal mode; the option set contributes nothing.

IM10-05.why: 35 restates the stem's percent as a degree count; 63 and 105 both fall below 120 degrees, which is one third of the circle, and the stem pins the sector above one third - only 126 survives that range.

IM10-06.why: 108, 36 and 12 stand in a 1 : 1/3 : 1/9 ladder; 108 is the stem's two givens multiplied (the unconverted area) and 36 applies the linear factor once, while the stem's own label says the conversion applies twice.

IM10-07.why: 2200, 2420 and 2662 are a geometric ladder each 1.1 times the last, i.e. the year-1, year-2 and year-3 balances; the stem asks for year 2, so the first and third rungs answer a different year.

IM10-08.why: 785 is exactly 314 + 471, the sum of two other options, which is the over-counted total; and 314 is a component corroborated inside both of the larger options, so a TOTAL surface area cannot equal it.

IM10-09.why: 12 and -12 form a sign pair whose magnitude requires both of Q's coordinates to sit at their extreme, which a reflection across an axis plus a 4-unit shift of the stem's small coordinates cannot produce; that leaves the two small values.

IM10-10.why: The set is the symmetric quartet +-2, +-0.5; the stem's two points move opposite ways so the sign is fixed as negative, but the option set alone gives no way to choose between the slope and its reciprocal.

IM10-11.why: Four small integers with no ladder, no restated given and no range the stem pins; nothing is eliminable.

IM10-12.why: 1130.4 is exactly three times 376.8 and the stem prints a formula containing a factor of 1/3, so 1130.4 is the un-thirded cylinder value and cannot be the cone's volume.

IM10-13.why: 16 is the two givens added and answers a different question; 2.5 and 5 are a doubling pair standing for 'the centre' and 'twice the centre', and the stem asks for the SUM of two symmetric solutions, so the larger of that pair is the one the stem selects.

IM10-14.why: 14 and 15 are adjacent integers and the stem asks for the LEAST integer strictly greater than a bound, which is the construction that produces exactly such a pair with the upper one as the answer; 28 is the doubling of 14 and 15 is also the stem's own constant, so the pair is the whole contest.

IM10-15.why: 150 and 450 are a 1:3 pair and the stem's ratio numerator is 3, so 150 is the one-part partial; 400 divides the population by the ratio's numerator rather than its denominator and answers nothing the stem asks.

IM10-16.why: Four weekday names carry no numeric structure, no ordering the stem pins and no restated given.

IM10-17.why: 21 is a raw given restated; 15 and 24 differ by exactly 9 and read as the before and after range LEVELS, while the stem asks by how much the range INCREASES, so the option equal to the difference of the other two is the only one answering the question asked.

IM10-18.why: A range of 2, and arguably 9, is impossible for a display whose stems already span three tens-groups, so only the two options above 10 remain legal.

IM10-19.why: In the stem's ratio the largest part exceeds the other two combined, so the largest angle must exceed 90 degrees; 75 and 84 are below that floor and are illegal without any arithmetic on the total.

IM10-20.why: A sum of two positive quantities must exceed each of them, so 1/24 (the product form) is illegal; 1/11 inverts the composite numerator that 11/24 carries and cannot be a sum of the two named terms.

IM10-21.why: 26 and 16 are exactly twice each of the stem's two coordinates, the signature of the 'reflected the same point' error; the option set encodes its own givens and the sum-of-magnitudes option is the one a cross-zero distance takes.

IM10-22.why: 7/40 implies a whole of 720 degrees, outside the circle the stem pins; 1/3 assumes equal sectors, which the stem's three unequal angles forbid; 2/5 is the share of the largest sector, answering about the wrong sector.

IM10-23.why: 8 is the stem's stated old median and adding a value larger than every listed number cannot leave the median unchanged; 10 is the average of two other options, which is the form a median of an even-sized set takes.

IM10-24.why: 121 is the given restated; 11, 22 and 44 are a 1:2:4 ladder, and a perimeter must be four times a side, so only the top rung can be the perimeter of a square whose side is the bottom rung.

IM10-25.why: 34, 36 and 38 are a tight arithmetic ladder and 16 is a magnitude outlier roughly half the ladder; nothing in the option set separates the three ladder members.

IM10-26.why: The stem asks for a count of perfect squares inside an interval whose upper end is barely past the seventeenth square, and the lower end removes the first several, so counts of 17 and 18 exceed the ceiling the stem pins; 11 and 12 are an off-by-one endpoint pair the options cannot split.

IM10-27.why: Every option is a plausible year-over-year gap for the magnitudes listed; deciding which are real differences and which is fabricated needs the subtraction the adaptation forbids.

IM10-28.why: 100 is not divisible by the stem's larger factor and 102 is not divisible by its smaller one, so both are illegal outright; 120 is legal as a multiple but is larger than 108, and the stem asks for the LEAST.

IM10-29.why: 25 restates the given minutes as degrees; a span of more than a third of an hour must exceed 120 degrees of a full turn, which kills 12.5, 25 and 90 on the range the stem pins.

IM10-30.why: The triangle inequality against the stem's hypotenuse and short leg forces the other leg above 18, so 18 and 12.5 (which is merely half a given) are illegal; the option set cannot separate the two survivors except by the familiar triple.
